section_summary: The section begins with a fragment of an Industrial Reconstruction Corporation law and a longer draft law reorganizing it as a public corporation. The remaining documents concern the 1948 Strike report on Japanese industrial reparations, State Department deliberations over Japan’s industrial level, and reactions reported from Manila and Shanghai. Chinese press translations show both opposition to Japanese industrial recovery and support for recovery under controls against renewed militarism.

subfiles.title: Law Concerning the Industrial Reconstruction Corporation
subfiles.about: Establishes the corporation’s purpose, legal status, registration, taxation, and officers.
subfiles.summary: The surviving opening provisions describe a corporation intended to use industrial equipment and materials for postwar rehabilitation. They set rules for offices, incorporation, registration, taxes, dissolution, and senior officers; the text breaks off during the directors’ duties.

subfiles.title: The Industrial Reconstruction Public Corporation Law
subfiles.about: Reorganizes the Industrial Reconstruction Corporation as a public corporation.
subfiles.summary: The draft defines the public corporation’s capital, officers, business, accounts, and supervision under the Economic Stabilization Board and competent minister. It covers construction, purchase, lease, and sale of industrial equipment and materials, with inspection powers and penalties. Supplementary provisions transfer the predecessor corporation’s rights and obligations to the new body.

subfiles.title: Request for Strike mission reports
subfiles.about: Requests the completed and forthcoming Strike mission reports.
subfiles.summary: Knowland asks for the Japanese reparations report immediately and the second report when available.

subfiles.title: Reply to Senator Knowland on Strike reports
subfiles.from: Charles E. Bohlen, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Explains where the Strike reports are held.
subfiles.summary: Bohlen says the Army supplied the first report and has not yet received the Overseas Consultants report.

subfiles.title: Request by Senator Knowland for copies of Strike reports
subfiles.about: Coordinates responses to Knowland’s requests.
subfiles.summary: Wisner reports agreement with Draper on handling the requests and suggests supplying contextual studies with the earlier report.

subfiles.title: Conversation with New Zealand counselor G. R. Powles
subfiles.about: Records questions about Japan’s peace settlement and occupation policy.
subfiles.summary: Powles urges progress on industry, reparations, raw material imports, and trade while peace talks remain uncertain.

subfiles.title: Need for technical advisory opinion on OCI report
subfiles.about: Proposes engineering review of technical claims in the OCI report.
subfiles.summary: Whitman proposes asking the Engineers Joint Council to assess disputed capacity and power industry estimates.

subfiles.title: Request for reparations survey and Pauley report
subfiles.about: Requests copies of Japanese reparations studies.
subfiles.summary: Doane asks urgently for the OCI survey, Pauley report, and related documents.

subfiles.title: Reply to Robert R. Doane
subfiles.about: Responds to a request for reparations reports.
subfiles.summary: Whitman encloses related releases, says Pauley copies are exhausted, and directs the OCI request to the Army.

subfiles.title: Need for technical advisory opinion on OCI report
subfiles.about: Responds to Whitman’s proposed independent engineering review.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum favors asking OCI’s authors for clarification before referring disputed points to outside engineers.

subfiles.title: Public reaction to Strike report
subfiles.to: Selected American diplomatic and consular officers
subfiles.about: Requests reports of public responses to Strike’s recommendations.
subfiles.summary: Posts are asked to report press and public reaction to the newly released reparations recommendations.

subfiles.title: FEC papers on level of Japanese industry
subfiles.about: Responds to a request for comment on FEC papers.
subfiles.summary: Thorp says instructions to General McCoy make further comment on the papers unnecessary.

subfiles.title: Request for concurrence on FEC industry papers
subfiles.about: Seeks comments on Butterworth’s memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Claxton forwards the FEC industry memorandum for concurrence or comments.

subfiles.title: Action on FEC papers on level of Japanese industry
subfiles.about: Recommends the U.S. stance on pending FEC industry proposals.
subfiles.summary: Wisner describes divisions among FEC delegates and possible upward revisions after the Strike report. He recommends making clear that the United States is uncommitted to the pending levels and unready to vote.

subfiles.title: British desire for FEC action on level of industry in Japan
subfiles.about: Records Hubert Graves’s proposal for an assured Japanese industrial floor.
subfiles.summary: Graves urges an early FEC guarantee of minimum industrial capacity, separate from reparations limits. Borton notes that this differs from his understanding of the U.S. position.

subfiles.title: Philippine press reaction to Strike report
subfiles.about: Reports local coverage of the Strike recommendations.
subfiles.summary: The embassy finds little reaction beyond a Manila Times editorial opposing reduced reparations and fearing renewed Japanese strength.

subfiles.title: Shanghai press reaction to Strike report
subfiles.about: Lists Shanghai newspaper coverage of the Strike report.
subfiles.summary: The consulate identifies articles, editorials, and wire reports, including objections in Ta Kung Pao and Shun Pao, and promises the March 25 editorial in full.

subfiles.title: Press reaction to the Strike report on Japanese reparations
subfiles.about: Transmits a Ta Kung Pao editorial.
subfiles.summary: Cabot says the editorial views the Strike plan as a threat to China and calls for protest.

subfiles.title: Ta Kung Pao editorial on Strike’s report
subfiles.about: Argues that the Strike plan would preserve Japanese war potential.
subfiles.summary: The editorial objects to using manufactured goods as reparations, raising Japan’s effective industrial level, and retaining capacity in metals, oil, chemicals, and shipping. It warns that the plan threatens Chinese security and calls for a Chinese protest.

subfiles.title: Editorial comment on Strike program for Japanese reparations
subfiles.about: Transmits contrasting Shanghai editorials on Japanese recovery.
subfiles.summary: Cabot forwards a critical editorial on U.S. recovery plans and an official Kuomintang editorial broadly supporting peaceful Japanese recovery under controls against militarism.

subfiles.title: Shanghai press review: Effort to Help Japan to Recover Becomes More Positive
subfiles.about: Provides extracts from Shanghai editorials, chiefly on U.S. plans for Japan.
subfiles.summary: The principal Tung Nan Jih Pao extract criticizes Draper’s proposals as effectively ending reparations and privileging aid to Japan over China. The page also carries an unrelated extract on Chinese constitutional politics.

subfiles.title: Shanghai press review: Our Policy Toward Japan
subfiles.about: Presents an official Kuomintang editorial on policy toward Japan.
subfiles.summary: Chung Yang Jih Pao supports Japanese self-sufficiency and peaceful trade if militarism remains controlled, praises MacArthur’s occupation policy, and favors an early peace treaty. Other press-review extracts begin on page 120.

subfiles.title: Consideration of SC 242/25 on Japanese industry
subfiles.about: Reports FEC Steering Committee debate on Japanese industrial levels.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum records delegation positions and disagreement over whether industrial ceilings should leave room for additional reparations removals. China and France favor that flexibility; Britain objects to linking industry levels to reparations. The committee postpones detailed consideration of Chinese amendments.

subfiles.title: Statement by Chinese member on policy toward Japanese industry
subfiles.about: Argues for balancing Japan’s peaceful industrial needs with reparations claims.
subfiles.summary: The speaker says industrial levels and reparations removals are inseparable under the Potsdam Declaration. The statement questions proposed capacity levels, seeks fuller technical and reparations review, and resists an immediate vote on SC 242/19.

subfiles.title: Strike reparations program
subfiles.about: Transmits a Sin Wen Pao editorial criticizing U.S. policy.
subfiles.summary: Cabot forwards an editorial comparing aid to Japan with proposals to extend the Marshall Plan to Spain.

subfiles.title: A Study of U.S. Policy Toward Japan
subfiles.about: Criticizes U.S. aid and industrial policy toward Japan.
subfiles.summary: The editorial fears that loans, liberal reparations policy, and preserved industry will rebuild Japanese militarism. It attributes U.S. policy partly to conflict with the Soviet Union and urges China’s government to object.

subfiles.title: Shanghai press review: A Study of U.S. Policy Toward Japan and other editorials
subfiles.about: Repeats the Sin Wen Pao editorial and continues with Chinese political extracts.
subfiles.summary: A second copy of the April 2 Sin Wen Pao editorial is followed by extracts on National Assembly seats and public funds. The press review continues beyond page 130.
